problem: Pre-trained visual representations (PVRs) for embodied AI (R3M, MVP, VIP, CLIP, OVRL) were each built and evaluated in one narrow domain, with different SSL objectives, pre-training data and downstream protocols. Their results cannot be compared, so nobody knew whether a single general-purpose 'visual cortex' existed, or whether MVP's positive scaling trend for manipulation holds across embodied AI.
motivation: A universal visual backbone that serves navigation, manipulation and locomotion would be a real foundation model for embodied agents. Biological organisms have one visual cortex, not one per task. The key observation is that the locally-best PVRs differ sharply in the size and type of their pre-training data (CLIP on 400M web image-text pairs, MVP on 4.5M egocentric frames). That raises the question of whether scaling model size, data size and data diversity can yield one PVR that is best everywhere.
key_idea: Fix the downstream policy-learning protocols on a 17-task, 7-benchmark suite (CortexBench) so that only the frozen visual encoder varies. Then train MAE ViT-B/L models on controlled mixes of egocentric video plus ImageNet (up to 5.6M frames) to study scaling. The largest model (VC-1) is then adapted per domain with either end-to-end fine-tuning or in-domain MAE.
insight: No PVR, including VC-1, dominates every benchmark. Scaling helps on average but not uniformly. Diversity matters more than size: adding navigation video (Ego4D+N) lifts ViT-L mean success 63.5→67.1, while the similar-sized Ego4D+M only reaches 64.4. Ego4D+MN is roughly on par with Ego4D+N (67.1→67.2) despite ~800K more frames, and adding ImageNet gives +1.5 (67.2→68.7). The adaptation ablation shows that the right strategy depends on how much downstream data exists. E2E fine-tuning helps large-scale IL/RL (ObjectNav 60.3→67.7, ImageNav 70.3→81.6, Mobile Pick 63.2→74.0) but collapses few-shot IL through overfitting (Adroit 59.3→15.9, DMC 66.9→6.7). MAE adaptation on the task's own frames helps few-shot IL (DMC 66.9→80.9) but slightly hurts navigation.
method: CortexBench: 17 tasks from 7 suites (Adroit, MetaWorld, DMControl, TriFinger, Habitat ObjectNav on HM3D, Habitat ImageNav on Gibson, Habitat 2.0 Mobile Pick), each with a fixed community-standard policy-learning protocol; reported metrics are Mean Success and Mean Rank.

Downstream protocols: few-shot BC with a 3-layer MLP on the ViT [CLS] token for MuJoCo/TriFinger (100 demos; 25 for MetaWorld); ObjectNav BC on 77k Habitat-Web human demos; ImageNav and Mobile Pick trained with RL (DD-PPO/VER, 500M steps). Nav/mobile-manipulation policies use ViT patch tokens through a compression layer into a 2-layer LSTM (navigation) or GRU (manipulation).
Pre-training data mixes: Ego4D (2.79M frames), +M (100DOH, SS-v2, Epic Kitchens), +N (OpenHouse24 139h home walkthroughs, RealEstate10K), +MN, +MNI (+ImageNet, 5.62M frames total).
MAE pre-training of ViT-B (86M) and ViT-L (307M) with default MAE hyperparameters; epochs are chosen so the number of updates matches MAE-on-ImageNet. VC-1 is the ViT-L trained on Ego4D+MNI.
E2E fine-tuning adaptation: VC-1 weights are updated jointly with the policy under the task loss (BC or RL), following the OVRL-V2 strategy.

MAE adaptation: VC-1 continues MAE training for 100 epochs on in-domain frames (expert-demo frames, or frames sampled from training environments for ImageNav/Mobile Pick), then is frozen for policy learning. An in-domain MAE baseline trained from random init serves as control.
Hardware proof-of-concept: few-shot BC on a real TriFinger (Push-Cube, 30 demos) and a Franka Panda (4 tasks, 30-250 teleoperated demos) using frozen or adapted VC-1.

setting.backbone: VC-1: MAE-pretrained ViT-L (frozen, E2E fine-tuned, or MAE-adapted) + task-specific policy (3-layer MLP for manipulation/locomotion BC; 2-layer LSTM for Habitat navigation; 2-layer GRU for Mobile Pick)
setting.training_data: Encoder: MAE pre-training on Ego4D+MNI, 5,621,987 frames (Ego4D 2.79M, 100DOH, SS-v2, Epic Kitchens, OpenHouse24, RealEstate10K, ImageNet 1.28M). Policies: ObjectNav BC on 77k Habitat-Web human demos (HM3D-Sem, 80 train scenes); ImageNav RL 500M steps on 72 Gibson train scenes; Mobile Pick RL 500M steps on ReplicaCAD; MuJoCo BC on 100 demos (25 for MetaWorld); TriFinger 100 demos; real robots 30-250 teleoperated demos
setting.observation: ImageNav: egocentric RGB 128x128 + goal image; ObjectNav: egocentric RGB 640x480 + proprioception (GPS/compass) + object category; Mobile Pick: egocentric RGB + proprioception + goal position; manipulation: RGB (+ proprioception)

numbers_note: Only SR is reported for the navigation tasks: no SPL, and no HM3D-ObjNav test-standard numbers. The split for Mobile Pick and the MuJoCo/TriFinger tasks is not named precisely; 'val' and 'test' are best guesses (the paper says MuJoCo results are rollouts on 'the test set'). For both navigation tasks the best checkpoint is selected by val SR, and results are reported on that same val split. There are internal inconsistencies. The random fine-tuned ViT-B baseline differs between Table 2 (DMC 43.5, TriFinger 56.1, ImageNav 62.5) and Table 3 (34.2, 55.0, 65.0). The text quotes 49.1 for scratch fine-tuning, while Table 2 shows 47.4. The VC-1 vs MVP gap is given as both +1.2 and +1.3. Frame counts for Ego4D+M and Ego4D+N are swapped between the appendix tables. Per-task success rates for all frozen models are in the appendix table 'The success rate for each task'. Model/data-scaling plots and rank distributions appear only in figures.
results: No existing PVR dominates. R3M is best on Adroit, MetaWorld and DMC; MVP ViT-L on TriFinger, ImageNav and Mobile Pick; CLIP on ObjectNav. Frozen VC-1 has the best mean success (68.7 vs MVP ViT-L 67.5) and the best mean rank (2.4), and beats CLIP on every benchmark, yet it is not best per task. Adaptation makes VC-1 competitive with or better than the best prior results everywhere: E2E fine-tuning reaches ObjectNav 67.7 (vs PIRLNav 70.4; best prior frozen PVR 54.4), ImageNav 81.6 (vs 82.0) and Mobile Pick 74.0. MAE adaptation reaches MetaWorld 96.0, DMC 80.9 and TriFinger 80.6. On real robots, VC-1 beats MVP (Franka 70.0 frozen / 85.0 MAE-adapted vs 55.0).
limitations: Only MAE and ViTs are studied for scaling; other SSL objectives or architectures may scale differently (R3M's ResNet still wins Adroit, MetaWorld and DMC when all models are frozen).

The adaptation that makes VC-1 competitive is per-benchmark, with separate in-domain training and hyperparameter tuning, so no single universal model reaches SOTA. Navigation results are SR-only on val splits with val-based checkpoint selection.
The simulated benchmarks are proxies; hardware experiments are small (12 trials for TriFinger, 40 for Franka).
